name: Jarmā al-Kubrā
history: Garama Metropolis was the royal capital of the Garamantes civilization. It served as the northern gateway and primary oasis emporium of the Central Trans-Saharan Trade Route, controlling subterranean irrigation channels (foggaras) that sustained caravan traffic carrying gold dust, ostrich feathers, salt, and exotic animals to Mediterranean ports.
idrisiHint: Navigate to Clime 1, Section 3. Look inland south of the Mediterranean coast of Tripoli into the Fezzan desert corridor.

name: Mamlakat al-Ḥabasha
history: Refers to the ancient Aksumite/Abyssinian Christian kingdom centered on the Tigray plateau and Eritrean highlands. Served as the crucial hinge between the African interior and Red Sea trade, exporting ivory, gold, frankincense, myrrh, emeralds, and civet through Adulis.
idrisiHint: Located in Clime 1, Sections 4 and 5. Find Bilād al-Ḥabasha positioned south (higher on the sheet) of Nubia and the Beja lands.

name: Dunqula min Bilād al-Nūba
history: Old Dongola was the fortified royal capital of the Christian Nubian kingdom of Makuria from the 6th to 14th centuries CE. Commanded major north-south riverine trade along the Nile and desert routes to Aidhab and the Darb al-Arba'īn trail.
idrisiHint: Located in Clime 1, Section 4. Trace the Nile River from the top downwards; Dunqula is prominently inscribed on the major bend of the river.

name: Kūshah al-Wāghilah
history: Preserves the ancient name of Kush and the Nile cataract settlement of Kosha. Situated along the Second and Third Cataracts, serving as a fortified customs terminal and transshipment port to bypass rapids.
idrisiHint: Located in Clime 1, Section 4. Positioned on the Nile bank north (downward) from Dongola toward the Egyptian border, labeled as Kūshah.

name: Saqlī / Simylla (Chaul)
history: Transcription of Greek Simylla (Sanskrit: Cemūla) on the Konkan coast of India. Received deep-water dhows arriving across the Arabian Sea carrying thoroughbred horses, dates, and frankincense, while exporting black pepper, teakwood, and muslins.
idrisiHint: Found in Clime 1, Section 8. Look along the western coastal strip of India south of the Gulf of Cambay and the Indus mouth.

name: al-Mayd min al-Sind
history: The Meds were an ancient seafaring, pastoral, and coastal population in the lower Indus delta and Makran coast. Dominated maritime transport, pilotage, and coastal cabotage between Makran, Daybul, and Cambay.
idrisiHint: Located in Clime 1 & 2, Section 8. Look along coastal pastures west and south of the Indus River between Tīz in Makran and Daybul/Mansura in Sindh.

name: ʿUmān (Dhofar)
history: Pinpoints Southern Oman (Dhofar/Zafār), the global center of the Frankincense Trade. Ports like Sumhuram, Mirbat, and Al-Baleed gathered resin harvested from Boswellia sacra trees to ship across the Indian Ocean.
idrisiHint: Located in Clime 1, Sections 6 and 7. Find the southern/eastern protrusion of the Arabian Peninsula bordering the Sea of Oman.

name: Qura min al-Hind (Ghogha / Khambhat)
history: Ancient Ptolemaic port district of Kora or Ghogha along the Gulf of Khambhat in Western India. Major trade nexus connecting Oman, Yemen, and the Persian Gulf with India for teak wood, spices, cotton textiles, and indigo.
idrisiHint: Located along the Gulf of Khambhat coast in Western India.

name: Madinat fi Safh Jabal (Gwalior)
history: Gwalior Fort or foothill fortress cities of the Malwa plateau in Madhya Pradesh. Key strategic defensive points and political centers contested by regional dynasties such as the Gurjara-Pratiharas.
idrisiHint: Situated along central Indian mountain ridge systems in Clime 2, Section 4–5.

name: Al-Ghamra min al-Sind
history: Located in the Lower Indus Valley (Sehwan / Hyderabad region, Pakistan). Important riverine and agricultural hinterland station along the Indus River corridor.
idrisiHint: Located along the lower Indus River inland from Daybul.

name: Al-Burur minhu 'ala al-Bahr (Berbera)
history: Coastal port city on the Somali seaboard. Served as a key commercial port and major trading center in the Somali Peninsula for Horn of Africa exports.
idrisiHint: Positioned along the Gulf of Aden coast on the Somali seaboard.

name: Al-Daybul / Debal
history: Founded in the 1st century CE, Banbhore/Debal became the most important trading port city in Sindh, housing thousands of Sindhi sailors including the Bawarij. Stone fortifications and citadel constructed under the Abbasids.
idrisiHint: Located near the Indus River delta mouth along the Arabian Sea.

name: Diyar Tali minhu (Yunnan / Dali)
history: Yunnan / Vietnam-China border region. Historically crossed by the Southwestern Silk Road connecting China to South Asia, rich in minerals (tin, copper, lead) and botanical diversity.
idrisiHint: Located at the eastern boundary limit of Clime 2.

name: Al-Yamama min al-Hijaz
history: Central Arabian plateau (Najd / modern Riyadh & Al-Kharj) centered around Hajar. Crucial agricultural center renowned across Arabia for its date palm orchards, wheat crops, and livestock.
idrisiHint: Inland central plateau of the Arabian Peninsula.

name: Ta'if min al-Yaman
history: Highland oasis city in the Sarawat mountains of the Mecca Province. Famous for agricultural produce, fruits, and strategic location guarding mountain routes to Mecca.
idrisiHint: Highlands east of the Red Sea coastal Tihama plain.

name: Makka min Tihama
history: Holiest city in Islam, site of the Kaaba and Al-Masjid al-Haram. Major sanctuary, pilgrimage destination, and trade hub in the Tihama coastal plain of Hijaz.
idrisiHint: Inland valley plain of Tihama in Western Arabia.

name: Yathrib Madinat al-Rasul
history: Situated in the volcanic oasis plateau of Hijaz. Destination of the Hijra in 622 CE, home to Al-Masjid al-Nabawi, and first political capital of the Islamic state.
idrisiHint: Volcanic oasis plateau of Northern Hijaz.

name: Akhmim min Sa'id Misr
history: Ancient Egyptian Ipu/Apu in Upper Egypt. Housed colossal ancient temples and extensive necropolises; served as an administrative and agricultural center along the Nile.
idrisiHint: Located on the east bank of the Nile River in Upper Egypt.

name: Ifriqiya min al-Gharb
history: Western Ifriqiya / Maghreb border region representing agricultural and political territories connecting Central North Africa to the Maghreb.
idrisiHint: Inland North Africa west of Tripolitania.

name: Bilad al-Samrani
history: Lower Euphrates basin (Sumerian region / Banu Shamran territory). Rich agricultural and canal zone in southern Mesopotamia.
idrisiHint: Lower riverine plain between Tigris and Euphrates.

name: Arandā min al-Ṣīn (Guangzhou / Canton)
history: Primary southern maritime gateway of China. Housed large foreign Muslim and Persian merchant communities; major shipyard center described by Odoric of Pordenone and Ibn Battuta.
idrisiHint: Far Eastern coastline at the southern terminus of Chinese trade routes.

name: Al-Qandahār min al-Hind
history: One of the oldest known urban settlements in Southern Afghanistan/Arachosia, functioning as a major Silk Road crossroads between Persia, Central Asia, and India.
idrisiHint: Southern Afghan plateau command post.

name: Kābul min al-Hind
history: Settlement over 3,500 years old controlling passes through the Hindu Kush mountains between Central Asia and the Indus Valley.
idrisiHint: High mountain basin in Eastern Afghanistan.

name: Rūyaḥ min Sijistān (Zaranj)
history: Capital of the Sistan basin. Strategic desert oasis emporium commanding trade along the Helmand River basin.
idrisiHint: Sistan basin oasis complex.

name: Barqa (Al-Marj, Libya)
history: Capital of Cyrenaica captured during early Arab conquests (643–644 CE). Prosperous Fatimid city exporting wool, honey, and fruit.
idrisiHint: North African coastal plain east of Tripoli.

name: Al-Sirḥān min Kermān (Sirjan)
history: Historical capital of Kerman province in southeastern Iran, controlling trade routes connecting the Iranian plateau to the Persian Gulf port of Hormuz.
idrisiHint: High plateau basin in Kerman province.

name: Shīrāz min Fārs
history: Largest metropolis of Fars province, embellished by Buyid ruler Adud al-Dawla with libraries, hospitals, palaces, and fortified military compounds. Birthplace of Syedna Moiyyad-al-Shirazi RA.
idrisiHint: Central Fars plain surrounded by Zagros peaks.

name: Al-Ahwāz min Khūzestān
history: Major river crossing and agricultural processing hub along the Karun River in Khuzestan.
idrisiHint: Khuzestan plain on the Karun River.

name: Al-Baṣrah min al-'Irāq
history: Garrison town founded in 636 CE under Caliph Umar. Evolved into a premier Islamic port, intellectual center, and commercial gateway to the Persian Gulf.
idrisiHint: Head of the Persian Gulf / Shatt al-Arab waterway.

name: Al-Kūfah min al-'Irāq
history: Relocated capital under Moulana Ali ibn Abi Talib AS (656 CE) and early seat of the Abbasids. Foundational center for Shia identity, home to the Great Mosque of Kufa, and namesake of Kufic script.
idrisiHint: Euphrates riverbank in central Iraq.

name: Dimashq min al-Shām
history: One of the oldest continuously inhabited cities in the world. Imperial capital of the Umayyad Caliphate (661–750 CE) and vital commercial crossroads along Levant trade routes.
idrisiHint: Barada River oasis at the foot of the Anti-Lebanon mountains.

name: Bayt al-Maqdis min Filasṭīn
history: Third holiest city in Islam, home to Al-Aqsa Mosque and Dome of the Rock built by Abd al-Malik in 691 CE. Central spiritual destination across Abrahamic traditions.
idrisiHint: Judean mountains between the Mediterranean and the Dead Sea.

name: Al-Fusṭāṭ min Miṣr (Old Cairo)
history: Founded in 641 CE by Amr ibn al-As; home to the first mosque built in Africa. Dynamic Fatimid economic engine, famous for ceramics (Fustat ware), glassmaking, and rag-paper trade preserved in the Cairo Genizah.
idrisiHint: East bank of the Nile River south of modern Cairo.

name: Al-Iskandariyyah
history: Historic Mediterranean port founded by Alexander the Great. Major maritime trade terminal connecting Nile-Red Sea commerce with the Mediterranean basin.
idrisiHint: Western edge of the Nile Delta on the Mediterranean coast.

name: Al-Qayrawān min al-Maghrib
history: Founded in 670 CE by Uqba ibn Nafi as the first major Islamic garrison city in North Africa. Outstanding spiritual, academic, and political capital of Ifriqiya.
idrisiHint: Inland plains of central Tunisia.

name: Ṭanjah min al-Maghrib
history: Strategic Maghrebi port commanding the Strait of Gibraltar. Western launching point for the 711 CE Arab-Berber expedition into Al-Andalus.
idrisiHint: Northwestern corner of Africa on the Strait of Gibraltar.

name: Samarkand
history: Commercial capital of Sogdia whose merchants dominated Silk Road trade. Site of the Islamic world's first industrial paper mill after the Battle of Talas (751 CE), replacing parchment across Abbasid administration.
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 8. Located in Sogdia north of the Oxus River, east of Bukhara.

name: Balkh
history: 'The Mother of Cities' (Umm al-Bilād). Site of the Nawbahār Buddhist monastery; ancestral home of the Barmakid vizierial family who funded Abbasid translation movements.
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 7/8. Placed south of the Oxus River at the northern foot of the Hindu Kush.

name: Herat
history: 'The Pearl of Khurasan' irrigated by qanāt canals from the Hari River. Tri-junction linking Iran, Central Asia, and Sistan; famous for brass inlay and patterned silks.
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 7. Located along the Hari River between Nishapur, Merv, and Balkh.

name: Merv
history: Oasis metropolis maintained by dams on the Murghab River. Imperial capital of Caliph al-Ma'mun (813–818 CE) during the 4th Fitna; famed for silk damask and ten major endowed libraries.
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 7. Terminal delta of the Murghab River in the Karakum Desert.

name: Nishapur
history: Controlled the ancient Madan turquoise mines supplying China and Byzantium. Major center for slipware epigraphic ceramics and home to Omar Khayyam, al-Ghazali, and Imam Muslim.
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 7. Western approaches of Khurasan at the base of the Binalud mountains.

name: Jurjan
history: Shielded by the 195km Great Wall of Gorgan. Capital of the Ziyarid dynasty (site of the 1006 CE Gonbad-e Qabus brick tower); location where Avicenna and al-Biruni wrote foundational medical and historical texts.
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 6/7. Coastal flatlands southeast of the Caspian Sea.

name: Amol
history: Primary city of Tabaristan defending Persian Zoroastrian traditions and later Zaydi Shi'ism. River port on the Haraz River exporting raw silk and timber to the Volga-Caspian Rus trade; birthplace of historian al-Tabari.
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 6. Between the Caspian shore and the northern slopes of Mount Damavand.

name: Rayy
history: 'The Bride of the World' (ʿArūs al-Dunyā). Central clearinghouse for Silk Road caravans; home to astronomer Abd al-Rahman al-Sufi and physician Rhazes (Abū Bakr al-Rāzī).
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 6. Plateau south of the Alborz mountains junction between Qazvin and Hamadan.

name: Daylam and Gilan
history: Mountain homeland of the Buyid dynasty who conquered Baghdad in 945 CE, providing the intellectual political shelter under which the Ikhwan al-Safa operated. Premier producer of high-grade raw silk (qazz).
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 6. Southwestern curve of the Caspian Sea.

name: Isfahan
history: Twin cities of Jayy (round administrative citadel) and al-Yahudiyya (Jewish artisan quarter). Famed for watered-silk taffeta; refuge where Avicenna spent 14 years completing Kitāb al-Shifā.
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 6. Irrigated valley of the Zayandeh River south of Rayy and Qom.

name: Hamadan
history: Ancient Ecbatana, capital of the Medes. Gatehouse of the Great Khurasan Road through the Zagros mountains where all overland traffic to Baghdad passed. Location of Avicenna's tomb.
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 6. High mountain plain at the base of Mount Alvand.

name: Baghdad
history: Founded in 762 CE by Caliph al-Mansur as the circular 'City of Peace' (Madīnat al-Salām). Home to the House of Wisdom (Bayt al-Hikma), catalyzing advances in algebra, optics, and medicine.
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 5. Labeled Madīnat al-Salām on the Tigris River, south of Samarra.

name: Mosul
history: 'The Junction Point' bridging Upper Mesopotamia with Iraq, Syria, and Armenia. Middle Eastern entrepôt market from which fine Indian Gossypium tree-cotton acquired its global trade name 'muslin'.
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 5. Western bank of the Tigris River directly opposite Nineveh.

name: Aleppo
history: Western terminus of the overland Silk Road where Central Asian caravans met Italian and Byzantine traders in limestone souks. Capital of Hamdanid emir Sayf al-Dawla, hosting al-Farabi.
idrisiHint: Clime 4, Section 4. Inland from Antioch and Latakia, west of the Euphrates.

name: Rumiya al-Kubra (Rome)
history: Westernmost European anchor of the 5th Clime, revered by medieval geographers as the historical capital of the Western Roman Empire and seat of the Papacy with stone aqueducts and basilicas.
idrisiHint: Clime 5, Western European section.

name: Maqadhuniyya (Macedonia)
history: Ancestral realm of Alexander the Great (Al-Iskandar / Dhul-Qarnayn), anchored by the port of Thessalonica guarding Balkan access corridors for the Byzantine Empire.
idrisiHint: Clime 5, European Balkan section.

name: Malatya min Arminiyya
history: Vital Muslim garrison fortress (Thaghr) along the frontier separating the Abbasid Caliphate from Byzantium. Staging ground for annual military expeditions into Anatolia.
idrisiHint: Clime 5, Upper Mesopotamian / Anatolian border.

name: Akhlat min Arminiyya
history: Situated on Lake Van; capital of the Shah-Armans dynasty serving as a Silk Road crossroads linking Transcaucasia, Azerbaijan, and Upper Mesopotamia.
idrisiHint: Clime 5, Lake Van shoreline.

name: Ardabil min Adharbayjan
history: Political and military capital of Azerbaijan province during the Umayyad and early Abbasid eras, controlling mountain passes leading to the Caspian Sea and Caucasus.
idrisiHint: Clime 5, High plateau near Mount Sabalan.

name: Al-Tiraz min Bilad al-Turk (Taraz)
history: Citadel on the Talas River along the Northern Silk Road. Site of the Battle of Talas (751 CE) where Abbasid forces defeated the Tang Chinese army.
idrisiHint: Clime 5, Talas River valley.

name: Bilad Khaqan min al-Turk (Semirechye)
history: Central royal steppe domain of the Turkic Khagan in the Chu and Ili river valleys (containing Suyab and Balasagun), representing the northern limit of settled civilization.
idrisiHint: Clime 5, Chu and Ili river basins.

name: Khwarazm
history: Agricultural oasis along the lower Amu Darya delta centered on Urgench. Birthplace of al-Khwarizmi (father of algebra) and al-Biruni.
idrisiHint: Clime 5, Amu Darya river delta.

name: Isbijab min al-Turk (Sayram)
history: Tax-exempt fortified frontier outpost (Ribat) guarding settled Transoxiana against northern steppe nomadic raids. Birthplace of Khoja Ahmed Yasawi.
idrisiHint: Clime 5, Northern frontier of Transoxiana.

name: Yajuj wa Majuj (Dzungarian Gate)
history: Northeastern frontier boundary associated with high mountain passes like the Dzungarian Gate on the Chinese border where Caliph Al-Wathiq sent the Sallam al-Tardjuman expedition.
idrisiHint: Clime 5, Extreme northeastern mountain barrier.
